plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In this format, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value of $36. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth if I win against a lower bid but higher than my value bid from others; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Truthful bidding maximizes expected profit since payment is determined by others' bids, not my own.

In a second-price auction, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), bidding exactly my value of $8 maximizes expected profit: I win whenever the second-highest bid is below $8 and pay only that amount, capturing positive surplus. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if others bid high; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Thus $8 is optimal.

This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). The dominant strategy in this format is to bid exactly my true value, $44. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth if others bid between my value and my bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. Since payment is determined by the second-highest bid, not my own bid, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies.
